questions.q: A holding company treats a group of legally separate subsidiaries that share common goals as one entity for architecture purposes. How does the TOGAF Standard view this arrangement?
o: It is invalid because an enterprise must be a single legal entity
An enterprise may itself comprise multiple enterprises linked by common goals
Each subsidiary must have a wholly separate framework
Only the parent company can be called an enterprise
questions.e: An enterprise is any collection of organizations with common goals and may comprise multiple enterprises, such as a holding company and its subsidiaries.

questions.q: Which three architecture domains are collectively referred to as the IT architecture?
questions.e: Data, Application, and Technology are often collectively called the IT architecture. Business is the fourth domain, kept separate.

questions.q: The TOGAF Standard states that the current and future states of the enterprise are described so that a particular element can be examined. What does that element represent?
o: The gap between the current and future states, showing what must change
questions.e: EA describes the baseline (current) and target (future) states; the gap between them identifies what must change to reach the goals.

questions.q: The Enterprise Continuum comprises which two complementary concepts?
o: The Baseline Continuum and the Target Continuum
The Architecture Continuum and the Solutions Continuum
The Strategic Continuum and the Segment Continuum
The Foundation Continuum and the Industry Continuum
questions.e: The Enterprise Continuum comprises the Architecture Continuum (reusable architecture building blocks) and the Solutions Continuum (solution building blocks).

questions.q: Which part of the Architecture Repository holds the standards with which new architectures must comply?
questions.e: The Standards Library holds standards new architectures must comply with, including industry standards, supplier products, and shared services.

questions.q: What is the key distinction between the Content Framework and the Architecture Repository?
o: The Content Framework stores work products; the repository defines them
The Content Framework defines which work products to develop; the repository stores the developed ones
They are two names for the same thing
The Content Framework applies only to Agile projects
questions.e: The Content Framework describes what to develop; the actual developed work products are stored in the Architecture Repository.

questions.q: In which ADM phase is the Architecture Capability established?
questions.e: The Architecture Capability, the ability to perform EA, is established in the Preliminary Phase and can be enhanced later.

questions.q: In a Gap Analysis matrix, what does an entry in the 'new' row represent?
o: Baseline building blocks that were intentionally eliminated
Target building blocks that must be developed or procured
Building blocks included in both baseline and target
questions.e: A target ABB missing from the baseline appears in the 'new' row and represents a gap to be developed or procured. The 'eliminated' column lists baseline items to shut down.

questions.q: How does the TOGAF Standard define risk?
o: A certain negative outcome of a project
The effect of uncertainty on objectives
The cost overrun of a migration project
A stakeholder concern that was ignored
questions.e: Risk is the effect of uncertainty on objectives, where uncertainty is any deviation from the expected, positive or negative. Risk has a probability and an impact.

questions.q: Which statement correctly places the Preliminary Phase and Requirements Management relative to the ADM cycle?
o: Both sit inside the A-H cycle as lettered phases
The Preliminary Phase precedes the cycle; Requirements Management sits at the centre
Requirements Management precedes the cycle; the Preliminary Phase is at the centre
questions.e: The Preliminary Phase precedes the A-H cycle; Requirements Management sits at the centre and operates continuously.

questions.q: Once a deliverable is approved, how may it subsequently be changed?
o: Any team member may edit it freely
Only through a change control or governance process
Only by returning to the Preliminary Phase
questions.e: Approved does not mean finalized. An approved deliverable may still evolve, but only through a change control or governance process.

questions.q: Which best characterizes the steps described within each ADM phase?
o: Mandatory instructions that must be followed in strict order
Recommendations to be tailored under architecture governance
Legal requirements enforced by the Open Group
questions.e: The steps within each phase are recommendations, not mandates. The ADM does not mandate a sequence or a waterfall; tailor it under architecture governance.

questions.q: Which of the following is a purpose of the Preliminary Phase?
o: Tailor the TOGAF framework to the enterprise
Finalize the Implementation and Migration Plan
Grant approval to proceed with the architecture project
questions.e: The Preliminary Phase creates the Architecture Capability, tailors the framework, and defines architecture principles.

questions.q: What critical gate marks the end of Phase A?
o: Finalization of the Architecture Requirements Specification
Approval to proceed with architecture development
questions.e: Phase A ends with approval to proceed, a critical gate. It defines scope, identifies stakeholders, and creates the vision.

questions.q: A project is developing the Data Architecture. Under the ADM, which other architecture is developed in the same phase?
questions.e: Phase C, Information Systems Architectures, covers both Data Architecture and Application Architecture.

questions.q: Which ADM phase develops the baseline and target Technology Architecture?
questions.e: Phase D develops the baseline and target Technology Architecture (the logical software and hardware infrastructure capabilities and standards).

questions.q: In Phase E, what does the term 'delivery vehicles' refer to?
o: Programs, projects, and portfolios that deliver the target
questions.e: Phase E identifies delivery vehicles, meaning the programs, projects, and portfolios through which the target architecture is delivered.

questions.q: What happens to the Implementation and Migration Plan in Phase F?
o: It is discarded and replaced by the roadmap
It is converted into a Change Request
questions.e: The Implementation and Migration Plan is first created in Phase E and finalized and approved in Phase F.

questions.q: What is the primary objective of Phase G, Implementation Governance?
o: To provide architectural oversight so implementation conforms to the target architecture
questions.e: Phase G provides architectural oversight of implementation, ensuring what is built aligns with the target architecture.

questions.q: A Change Request is received in Phase H. What are the two possible outcomes the phase decides between?
o: Approve the budget or reject the project
A light update to the architecture, or a full new ADM cycle
Escalate to the sponsor or archive the request
Start Phase A or start Phase E
questions.e: Phase H is a holding phase; a Change Request may trigger a light update to the architecture or warrant a full new ADM cycle.

questions.q: What does Requirements Management maintain as the single point of truth?
o: The complete set of architecture requirements with traceability
questions.e: Requirements Management maintains the complete requirement set as a single point of truth, providing traceability from vision and strategy down to detailed requirements.

questions.q: Who develops architecture principles, and who formally approves them?
o: The project managers develop and approve them
Enterprise architects with key stakeholders develop them; the Architecture Board approves them
The sponsor develops and approves them alone
External auditors develop and approve them
questions.e: Architecture principles are developed by enterprise architects together with key stakeholders and then approved by the Architecture Board.

questions.q: In the TOGAF template for an architecture principle, which section states the business benefits and guidance for balanced interpretation?
questions.e: The Rationale highlights the business benefits, relationship to other principles, and guidance for balanced interpretation. The four sections are Name, Statement, Rationale, Implications.

questions.q: A principle written with clear, unambiguous intentions so that violations are minimized meets which of the five criteria?
questions.e: Understandable means the intention is clear and unambiguous so violations are minimized. The five criteria are Complete, Consistent, Stable, Understandable, Robust.

questions.q: The desired outcomes captured in a business scenario should follow which model?
questions.e: Business scenario outcomes should be SMART: Specific, Measurable, Actionable, Realistic, and Time-bound.

questions.q: In which ADM phase is the Business Transformation Readiness Assessment applied, and where do its mitigations flow?
o: Phase G; into the Architecture Contract
Phase A; into the Implementation and Migration Plan
Phase H; into the Change Request
questions.e: The BTRA is applied in Phase A; the risk mitigations it identifies feed into the roadmap and the Implementation and Migration Plan in Phases E/F.

questions.q: The residual level of risk is best described as which of the following?
o: The risk categorization before any mitigation
The risk categorization after mitigating actions are applied
A risk that cannot be identified
A risk arising outside the transformation scope
questions.e: The residual level of risk is the categorization remaining after mitigating actions are applied; the initial level is before mitigation.

questions.q: What does iteration within an ADM cycle enable a project to do?
o: Remove the need for a baseline architecture
questions.e: Iteration within a cycle supports projects operating multiple ADM phases concurrently, for example managing the B/C/D interrelationships together.

questions.q: Which set correctly lists the three levels of the Architecture Landscape from broadest to most detailed?
questions.e: The three landscape levels are Strategic (broadest, long horizon), Segment (medium), and Capability (most detailed, short horizon).

questions.q: What is the rule for how far to partition an architecture?
o: Partition until it mirrors the organizational chart
Partition until each architecture has one owning team
Partition only when using Agile delivery
questions.e: Partition until each architecture has a single owning team, which removes unclear responsibilities and eliminates conflict.

questions.q: Which scoping dimension defines the planning horizon articulated for the vision?
questions.e: Time Period is the planning horizon for the vision, which must be achievable with available resources. The four dimensions are Breadth, Depth, Architecture Domains, and Time Period.

questions.q: Governance is best summarized as the system by which the enterprise is which of the following?
questions.e: Governance is the system by which the current and future state are directed and controlled. Architecture Governance is part of corporate governance.

questions.q: Where do the decision rights about the target architecture ultimately lie?
questions.e: Decision rights about the target architecture always lie with the stakeholders. The Architecture Board owns the processes and recommendations, not the decision rights.

questions.q: Which document is itself a type of Architecture Contract established in Phase A?
questions.e: The Statement of Architecture Work is a contract between the architecting organization and the sponsor and serves as a type of Architecture Contract.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a 'Non-conformant' level of architecture conformance?
o: The implementation has no features in common with the architecture
The implementation actively violates mandatory requirements
The implementation meets all mandatory requirements
The implementation is not subject to compliance review
questions.e: Non-conformant means the implementation actively violates one or more mandatory architectural requirements. This is the most severe conformance outcome; it triggers enforcement action.

questions.q: Which statement about an architecture viewpoint is correct?
o: It is specific to a single architecture and cannot be reused
It is generic and reusable, stored in a viewpoint library, and governs how a view is built
It is always expressed as a matrix
It replaces the need for stakeholder concerns
questions.e: A viewpoint is generic and reusable, defines the conventions for constructing and interpreting a view, and is stored in viewpoint libraries. The view is specific.

questions.q: How does the TOGAF Standard define a concern?
o: An interest in a system relevant to one or more stakeholders
A physical component of the architecture
questions.e: A concern is an interest in a system relevant to one or more stakeholders, covering areas such as performance, reliability, and security. Concerns lead to requirements.

questions.q: At which point in the ADM are selected Architecture Building Blocks refined into Solution Building Blocks?
questions.e: ABBs are identified in Phases A-D; selected ABBs are refined into SBBs (purchased or developed) in Phase E.

questions.q: Which deliverable documents the findings of Phase A and acts as the contract against which project execution is measured?
questions.e: The Statement of Architecture Work documents Phase A findings, specifies scope and approach, and is the document against which execution is measured.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the Communications Plan?
o: To trigger a new architecture cycle
To ensure the right architecture information reaches the right stakeholders at the right time
questions.e: The Communications Plan conveys architecture information to stakeholders within a planned, managed process, ensuring the right information reaches the right people at the right time. It is created in Phase A.
